dedupe_keys.name: climate adaptation risk assessment and resilience planning at heathrow airport 2011 and 2016 adaptation reports

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how Heathrow Airport Limited (HAL) assessed climate risks to the airport under the UK Climate Change Act 2008 reporting power. The 2011 adaptation report combined climate modelling for the short term (to 2020) and the medium to long term (2020 to the 2050s) under high, medium and low emission scenarios with literature review and consultation of the Environment Agency, NATS, the London Borough of Hillingdon, Transport for London, surface transport operators and airlines. It identified 34 risks in the worst case, with rain and flooding, temperature, fog and changing wind direction the conditions needing most attention, and sorted responses into action, prepare and watching brief classes. A progress report followed in July 2016, reporting all short-term actions done, and an operational resilience plan was prepared for the Civil Aviation Authority in 2014. The page, first published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML with links to Heathrow's pages. Caveats: the risk register itself is not published on the page, no costs are given beyond the rule that each action needs a cost-benefit analysis, and wind direction cannot yet be modelled probabilistically. The case illustrates climate adaptation and resilience planning for a hub airport and its interdependencies with utilities, fuel supply and surface access; related records are the Brazil ANAC air transport statistics and the OpenSky Network data.
name: Climate adaptation risk assessment and resilience planning at Heathrow Airport (2011 and 2016 adaptation reports)
outcomes: 34 climate risks were identified; all short-term actions from the 2011 report were implemented by the 2016 progress report, and weather was not expected to affect operations significantly to 2040.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from Heathrow Airport Limited and the Civil Aviation Authority
